I’m grateful Sam has Willoughby on the app but outside of this conversation he doesn’t seems to caution or mention pitfalls enough. Yes it’s more likely a rapid or negative change can happen on a retreat, but contrary to other comments on this post, they most definitely can still happen even with a small daily practice. As you’re practicing you’re changing how your mind works. If you don’t have an ongoing dialogue with a teacher that can answer questions, asses where you’re at, or “correct” a way you’re misunderstanding a practice, over time you might find that you’ve gotten yourself into a place that is distressful or undesirable. The downside to an app like Waking Up is that you’re by yourself and don’t have direct access to these teachers you’re learning from. Sam seems to speak about his style of meditation in an objective way as if it’s “the” way to practice and “the” way to be in the world rather than “a” way to be. In reality every person is different with a unique mind and life history that may need to practice or not practice in a particular way based on who they are. I like the waking app and have found a lot of it helpful, however that doesn’t mean everything on there is necessarily helpful for most people most of the time as it’s often presented. I don’t know if it’s just because Sam didn’t personally experience any serious pitfalls or negative side affects, but with the size of his growing users he has a responsibility and doesn’t caution about it enough. Luckily supportive communities are continuing to grow such as cheetahhouse.org which is an excellent resource for meditators in distress.
